image.description: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

item.title: Can the new PKK law bring peace to Turkey?
item.description: Turkey’s parliament has passed a framework law for the peace process with the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK). What does it stipulate, why is it controversial and what does it mean for the future of the peace process?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Hungary's parliament elects Orban critic as new president
item.description: Hungary's parliament has overwhelmingly confirmed Andras Baka, formerly the head of the Supreme Court, to the largely ceremonial role of president. New Prime Minister Peter Magyar controversially removed his predecessor.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Disrupted monsoons force India to face climate threat
item.description: For generations, India has lived by the rhythm of the southwest monsoon. But with the country hit by dry spells, cloudbursts and deadly floods, climate swings now expose the costs of building for yesterday's weather.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Key issues in Zambia's 2026 general election
item.description: Economic recovery, youth turnout, women's representation and judicial independence are among the issues shaping Zambia's vote on Thursday.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Bulgaria drone crash a wake-up call for country's defenses
item.description: The explosion of a Ukrainian decoy drone in Bulgaria near the Romanian border reveals gaps in Bulgaria's defenses, raises questions and shines a light on the country's policy shift on the war in Ukraine.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Trump pushes overhaul of US policy on vaccines for children
item.description: In an executive order, President Trump calls for fewer recommended childhood vaccinations and more spacing between shots. Medical experts say the changes lack scientific backing and could leave children less protected.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Turkey MPs back historic law on reintegrating PKK militants
item.description: Turkey's parliament has taken a major step toward ending four decades of conflict with the PKK. The new law sets out how some militants can return to civilian life, but leaves Abdullah Ocalan's future unresolved.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Colombia earthquake: Death toll rises to over 100
item.description: A powerful earthquake, measured at magnitude 7.4, has struck Colombia, killing dozens of people and trapping many under rubble. Cities including Cali, Pereira and Manizales were among the hardest-hit.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Which country is the new Mecca defense pact targeting?
item.description: Observers suggest the new alliance between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan won't result in any of the countries fighting for each other. Instead it's about preventing Iran and Israel from regional dominance, they say.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: How climate change is reshaping Africa's malaria risk
item.description: Researchers say warming temperatures are altering malaria transmission patterns across Africa, creating new challenges for health systems and disease control.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: ASEAN closing ranks as cyberscam threat escalates
item.description: Southeast Asian governments are searching for a joint strategy against cyberscammers, a criminal industry that has grown too big, too connected and too embedded in ASEAN economies to be solved just by policing.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: India: Anger over exam irregularities spreads to Jharkhand
item.description: Inspired by the Cockroach movement, young people in India's eastern state of Jharkhand are marching on the state assembly to demand transparency and a probe into alleged irregularities in civil service recruitment exams.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Thai ex-lawmaker shoots local official dead over loan
item.description: A former lawmaker confessed to shooting a senior official at a government office over a money dispute, police have said. The incident came just days after Thailand's deadliest shooting in nearly four years.
